results.title: Korea, UN agree to set up working group on peacekeeping contributions
results.content: Korea and the United Nations have agreed to establish a joint working group to discuss ways to expand Seoul's contributions to U.N. peacekeeping operations (PKO) following the planned withdrawal of its troops from Lebanon next year, the foreign ministry said Wednesday. The agreement was reached during separate meetings in New York on Monday (local time) between Chang Wook-jin, the ministry's coordinator-general for international organizations and global affairs, and Mohamed Khaled Khiari, U.N. assistant secretary-general for the Department of Peace Operations, and Atul Khare, under-secretary-general for the Department of Operational Support, according to the ministry. The working group will coordinate the safe withdrawal of the Dongmyeong unit from Lebanon and discuss ways to strengthen Korea's contributions to peacekeeping efforts. results.title: PM says Seoul's development aid will focus on helping partner nations grow on their own
results.content: Korea will focus its official development assistance (ODA) on helping recipient nations tackle problems on their own and grow, Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Wednesday. Han made the remark during a ceremony commemorating International Development Cooperation Day that marks South Korea's accession in 2009 to the OECD Development Assistance Committee, the first case of a recipient nation joining the grouping of rich countries. "The number of places in need of assistance continues to grow due to conflicts, climate disasters, famine and diseases while at the same time, the financial resources remain limited, leaving us with the task of how to maximize the impact of our support," Han said. "For us to address this together, partner nations must develop the capacity to solve their own problems and grow," she said. results.title: Remains of Korean Army corporal killed in Vietnam War to be returned home
results.content: The remains of a Korean soldier who died while serving in the Vietnam War will return home, marking the repatriation 59 years after his death, the defense ministry said Wednesday. The ceremony marking the return of late Army Cpl. Ahn Gyu-tae will take place at Seoul Airport in Seongnam, south of Seoul, overseen by Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul, according to the ministry. His remains will be transferred home from Hawaii via the Air Force's C-130 aircraft, it added. Ahn, who served as an Army corporal under the 9th Infantry Division, was deployed to Vietnam in August 1966 in the midst of the war between communist-backed North Vietnam and the United States and its allies, including South Vietnam and Korea. results.title: UNESCO spotlights Korea's cultural heritage in new global video series
results.content: A new UNESCO video series is bringing Korea’s cultural heritage to a global audience, showcasing ancient temples, historic villages and living traditions in a campaign that has already begun attracting attention through the international organization’s digital platforms. The fourth season of the UNESCO World Heritage Series, titled “Korea: A journey through time,” is being released in installments on UNESCO’s official Instagram, YouTube and other social media channels through Dec. 22, the Korea Heritage Service said Wednesday. The series, supported by the Korea Heritage Service and the World Heritage Interpretation and Presentation Centre (WHIPIC), features six World Heritage sites and three elements of Korea’s intangible cultural heritage. results.title: Father Ham Je-doe, who made more than 60 trips to North Korea, dead at 93
results.content: CHEONGJU — Father Ham Je-doe, born Gerard Hammond, an American Maryknoll missionary who spent more than six decades in Korea and devoted himself to humanitarian work in North Korea, died Monday. He was 93. The Diocese of Cheongju announced that Father Hammond, who had been hospitalized at Cheongju St. Mary's Hospital due to age-related illness, died at 7:46 a.m. Monday. Born in Philadelphia in 1933, Hammond graduated from Maryknoll Seminary and was ordained a priest before choosing Korea as his first mission destination in 1960. After arriving in Korea, he served as director of the Sacred Heart Orphanage in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, caring for children. He later spent more than 30 years conducting pastoral work in the Diocese of Cheongju, dedicating himself to evangelization and social service in the region. results.title: Retail sales rise 5.7% in October on steady online sales
results.content: Korea's retail sales rose in October from a year earlier on solid sales from online platforms, government data showed Wednesday. Combined sales of 26 major retail companies increased 5.7 percent from a year earlier, according to data by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources. Offline retailers reported a 1.4 percent decrease in sales due mainly to sluggish sales in large discount outlets as the Chuseok holiday fell in September this year. Last year, the Korean equivalent of Thanksgiving Day was in October based on the lunar calendar. Revenue at major online retail platforms rose a solid 10.9 percent from a year earlier in October on steady demand for food and delivery services. Online platforms accounted for 60.3 percent of total retail sales in October.

results.title: Changwon court judges to discuss judicial independence
results.content: Judges at a district court in the southeastern city of Changwon are set to meet Wednesday to discuss judicial independence amid the ruling Democratic Party of Korea's (DPK) push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, legal sources said. The regular general meeting of all judges at the Changwon District Court was scheduled to take place in the afternoon, with independence of the judiciary on the agenda, according to the sources. The session comes after the DPK said last week it will seek Cho's impeachment, accusing the top court of failing to properly respond to former President Yoon Suk Yeol's botched 2024 martial law bid among other reasons. Some judges across the nation have voiced criticism against the DPK's move. results.title: Samsung SDI Ulsan plant earns top green management award
results.content: Samsung SDI said Wednesday that its Ulsan plant has won the Grand Prize at the 2026 Green Management Awards, organized by the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute (KEITI). The plant received the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Award in the Excellent Green Company category, which recognizes companies demonstrating outstanding environmental management in areas such as carbon neutrality and resource conservation. The Green Management Awards recognize exemplary achievements in environmental management, environmental information disclosure and environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices. results.title: Undefeated Utah football brings American college tradition to Korea
results.content: INCHEON, South Korea — The University of Utah Asia Campus will host a community football watch party in Songdo, Incheon, on Nov. 28, bringing students, alumni, local residents and international families together as the Utah Utes pursue a historic undefeated season. The event will begin at 11 a.m. at Chris Ireland Hall (Room U104) on the University of Utah Asia Campus, featuring Utah's regular-season finale against West Virginia University. The gathering aims to introduce American college football culture while strengthening ties between the university and its surrounding community. Utah enters the game with an 11-0 record, standing as the only remaining undefeated team in the NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision (FBS), the highest level of American college football. results.title: Handong partners with Korea Mediation Institute to promote mediation education
results.content: The Handong International Law School (HILS) and the Handong Institute for Arbitration and Reconciliation (HIAR) have signed a memorandum of understanding with the Korea Mediation Institute (KMI) to expand academic and practical collaboration and enhance students’ mediation skills. Handong Global University said the agreement was signed on Nov. 11 by HILS Dean Lee Hee-eun, HIAR President Shin Eun-joo and KMI President Moon Yong-ho. HILS and HIAR are affiliated with the university. The partnership aims to draw on the expertise and resources of the three institutions to advance mediation education, promote joint research and help develop mediation practices. Under the agreement, the three institutions will jointly develop and offer courses, lectures, workshops and practical programs in mediation and negotiation. results.title: Global Public Procurement Marketplace kicks off in Seoul
results.content: An event aimed at helping Korean companies connect with overseas procurement markets kicked off its two-day run in Seoul on Wednesday, the Public Procurement Service (PPS) said. The Global Public Procurement Marketplace 2026, co-hosted by the PPS, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency and KEPCO KPS, brings together over 110 prospective buyers and more than 330 local companies, the PPS said. This year, PPS has placed particular emphasis on expanding opportunities for domestic companies to enter new overseas public procurement markets, including those of international organizations, and supporting export market diversification. results.title: Korea slashes nationality reinstatement wait times to 9 months for ethnic Koreans living abroad
results.content: The Ministry of Justice has significantly accelerated the nationality reinstatement process for ethnic Koreans living abroad, cutting the average review time by four months — from 13 months down to nine. For applicants experiencing the fastest processing, wait times have been reduced by as much as seven months, offering swift relief to thousands eager to formally reconnect with their homeland. The breakthrough stems from an intensive, three-month processing campaign conducted between August and October, according to the ministry. Facing a growing backlog fueled by a steady rise in applications from ethnic Koreans living abroad, the ministry overhauled its operational capacity. Previously, a single dedicated officer handled the workload, processing an average of roughly 220 cases per month. results.title: Late firefighter in Bucheon factory blaze named person of national merit
results.content: A firefighter killed in the line of duty while battling a factory fire in a city southwest of Seoul last month has been registered as a person of national merit, the veterans ministry said Wednesday. The decision was finalized upon approval by a review committee of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs on Friday and his bereaved family was notified earlier this week, according to the ministry. Fire Lt. Kim Jin-seok died from severe injuries sustained while battling a blaze that broke out at a metalworking factory in Bucheon, just west of Seoul, on Oct. 16. Six other firefighters were also injured. Kim's death sparked calls for a review of firefighting protocols amid questions over whether crews should be rushed into containment efforts without properly assessing the scene to minimize on-site risks to personnel. results.title: Kim Ha-seong signs with Detroit Tigers: reports
results.content: Korean infielder Kim Ha-seong has reportedly signed with the Detroit Tigers, his fourth team in four years in Major League Baseball (MLB). ESPN.com first reported Tuesday (U.S. local time) that Kim had agreed to a one-year deal worth $5 million. According to MLB.com, the deal, pending a physical, includes another $1 million in performance-based incentives. The Tigers have not confirmed the signing as of this writing. Kim played for the San Diego Padres from 2021 to 2024 and enjoyed his best campaign in 2023, when he won a National League Gold Glove at the utility spot and set career highs with 17 home runs, 60 RBIs, 38 steals and a .749 on-base plus slugging. Now 31, Kim has not been the same player since hurting his right shoulder late in the 2024 season. results.title: Korea's consumer goods exports hit record high amid Korean culture boom
results.content: Exports of Korean beauty, food, fashion and cultural products hit a record high amid the global popularity of Korean culture as the country's total exports surpassed $1 trillion for the first time, customs data showed Wednesday. Shipments of such Korean consumer goods totaled $28.65 billion from January through Thursday, when the country hit the export milestone, according to data from the Korea Customs Service. The figure marked a 21.5 percent spike from the same period last year and already surpassed last year's full-year total of $27.02 billion. Exports of beauty products surged 34.6 percent on-year to $13.65 billion over the cited period on steady demand for Korean cosmetics. This accounted for 47.6 percent of total consumer goods exports. In 2025, exports of beauty products totaled $11.61 billion, accounting for 43 percent of the total. Outbound shipments of Korean food increased 9.

results.title: North Korea to consider shutting down Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang, KCNA says
results.content: North Korea condemned Switzerland on Tuesday for sanctioning a North Korean children's camp over the transfer of children from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine and said it would consider shutting down the Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang, state media said. North Korean leader Kim Jong-un's influential sister, Kim Yo Jong, said the Swiss sanctions infringed on the country's sovereignty and demonstrated hostility towards Pyongyang, KCNA state news agency reported. Voice of America reported last week that Switzerland had added North Korea's Songdowon International Children's Camp to its sanctions list for cooperating with Russia-linked groups to transfer children from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine. results.title: Can renewable energy really get cheaper?
results.content: Every time you ask a chatbot a question, a data center somewhere uses electricity. The International Energy Agency expects global data center electricity consumption to more than double by 2030 as artificial intelligence (AI) spreads. That would be more electricity than the entire country of Japan uses today. In the United States, people living near clusters of data centers are angry as their household electricity bills rise. In Europe, some factories are shutting down because power has become too expensive. The cost of electricity is becoming everyone's problem. Korea is no exception. New semiconductor factories and AI data centers are driving electricity demand up again. Yet Korea imports more than 90 percent of its energy. results.title: Bourse operator activates sell-side sidecar for KOSPI on sharp fall
results.content: Korea's bourse operator on Wednesday activated a sell-side sidecar for the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) as the market came under heavy selling pressure. Program trading for the KOSPI-listed shares was suspended for five minutes from 9:09 a.m., according to the Korea Exchange (KRX). This comes as investors tracked overnight losses in technology stocks on Wall Street. A sell-side sidecar is triggered when the KOSPI 200 Futures Index falls 5 percent or more for at least one minute.

results.title: Seoul shares down over 5% late Wednesday morning on tech rout
results.content: Korean shares extended their losses late Wednesday morning, reversing the previous session's rally, as investors tracked overnight losses in technology stocks on Wall Street. After opening a sharp 3.94 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) extended its losses, shedding 277.22 points, or 5.54 percent, to 4,728.81 as of 11:20 a.m., and falling below the psychologically important 5,000 mark. As the market lost ground, the Korea Exchange activated a sell-side sidecar at 9:09 a.m., suspending buy orders in program trading for KOSPI-listed shares for five minutes. On Tuesday, the KOSPI rebounded more than 6 percent as chipmakers rallied amid a global wave of optimism sparked by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return to the spotlight. results.title: Chinese tech giant Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, US jury finds
results.content: NEW YORK — A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiring to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks as it grew into one of the world’s biggest suppliers of gear for wireless telecommunications networks. But jurors acquitted Huawei of the most serious charge: engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy, a result that the company's lawyer said was a “profound rejection” of the government's narrative that it was corrupt from top to bottom and had a corporate culture of cheating, stealing and lying. Prosecutors had used the charge, commonly found in organized crime and drug cases, to accuse Huawei of operating illicitly to poach intellectual property and technological secrets from competitors and partners. results.title: N. Korea's Yongbyon nuclear complex expansion may boost weapons-grade uranium production, says US science institute
results.content: WASHINGTON — North Korea's latest expansion of a uranium enrichment facility at its Yongbyon nuclear complex may be aimed at increasing its production of weapons-grade uranium, a U.S. research institute assessed Tuesday. The Washington-based Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS) made the assessment in a report based on satellite imagery of the facility, located some 100 kilometers north of Pyongyang, whose rapid expansion has drawn concern from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). The institute said satellite imagery of the newly built extension indicated that it consists primarily of a large hall without internal dividing walls, raising the possibility that it could accommodate additional uranium enrichment equipment. results.title: Biz sentiment drops for the first time in 5 months
results.content: Korea's business sentiment fell for the first time in five months in November due mainly to sluggish sales and rising inventory, a central bank survey showed Wednesday. The Composite Business Sentiment Index (CBSI) for all industries stood at 103.5 in November, down 0.7 point from the previous month, according to data from the Bank of Korea (BOK). The reading marked the first on-month decline since June, when the index dropped 1.2 points. The index measures corporate outlooks on overall business conditions, with a reading above 100 indicating that optimists still outnumber pessimists. The CBSI among manufacturers fell 0.8 point on-month to 104.8 in November from a more than four-year high of 105.6 the previous month. results.title: Seoul Metro labor, management reach last-minute deal to avoid strike
results.content: Labor and management at Seoul Metro reached a last-minute agreement on wages and working conditions Wednesday, avoiding a planned general strike that could have disrupted the morning commute, according to labor and management representatives. All three labor unions at Seoul Metro, which operates subway Lines 1-8 and part of Line 9, reached agreements with management and called off their planned general strike, which had been scheduled to begin with the first trains of the day. The two sides agreed to cap wage increases at 3.5 percent, while management will put on hold its existing restructuring plan to eliminate 2,212 jobs and hire 500 new employees Union 1, 2 and 3 have 9,100, 2,560 and 2,220 members, respectively. results.title: Naver to invest $743 mil. in logistics amid intensifying Coupang rivalry
results.content: Naver plans to invest nearly 1 trillion won ($743.7 million) in logistics infrastructure by 2030 as it moves to strengthen its delivery capabilities and take on Coupang in Korea’s increasingly competitive e-commerce market. The tech giant will be launching a new logistics subsidiary this year, with its Chief Operating Officer Kim Bom-jun tapped to lead the unit as its first CEO. The subsidiary will take the lead in designing logistics systems and infrastructure, while Naver will continue to rely on existing partners to operate warehouses and handle deliveries. The move addresses a longstanding weakness in Naver's e-commerce business — delivery speed and consistency — as the company seeks to strengthen its position following a massive data breach last year at rival Coupang. results.title: Disney's 'Hexed' blends vibrant magic with heartfelt family story
results.content: Walt Disney Animation Studios' 65th animated feature, "Hexed," arrives in Korean theaters Wednesday with vibrant visuals, witty creature design and a tender story at its center, even if its plot follows a familiar formula. Co-directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand and Josie Trinidad, the animated feature introduces Billie Doe (voiced by Hailee Steinfeld), an impulsive 16-year-old navigating the awkwardness of suburban life. Everything changes when a magic-suppressing bracelet accidentally unlocks on her wrist, unleashing dormant powers and opening a portal into Hexe, a sprawling realm inhabited by witches. Pulled into this world alongside her overprotective mother, Alice (Rashida Jones), Billie quickly realizes that Hexe is no carefree wonderland. results.title: Korea's 4,500-kilometer coastline walking trail celebrates decade of scenic journeys
results.content: Discovering Korea on foot offers an intimate look at the country that high-speed trains and city itineraries simply cannot match. Stretching roughly 4,500 kilometers across 284 courses — nearly three times the length of Spain’s famed Camino de Santiago — the "Korea Dulle Trail" traces the nation’s entire coastline and northern frontier, turning long-distance walking into one of Korea’s signature travel trends. As the trail marks its 10th anniversary this year, the Korea Tourism Organization (KTO) is highlighting the route as a bucket-list slow-travel experience and recently named beloved comedian Hwang Je-seong as its new honorary ambassador to promote the trail. Hwang will officially step into the role during an appointment ceremony at Seoul Marina Club & Yacht in Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, Wednesday. results.title: From local comfort food to global franchise: Chinese malatang king's Korea test
results.content: At around 7 p.m. on a recent Monday, more than half of the dozen or so tables were occupied at a Yangguofu Malatang restaurant in Yeoksam, an office-packed area in Seoul's Gangnam District. Vegetables, fish balls, rice cakes and instant noodles lined a refrigerated self-service topping bar, while pickled radish, peanuts and dipping sauces were available nearby. Two employees juggled cooking, payments, serving and clearing tables in the orange-hued restaurant. Yangguofu Group, one of China's largest malatang chains with nearly 7,000 outlets worldwide, has grown its overseas network from just over 20 in early 2023 to more than 200 across 30 countries and territories, as it steps up its global expansion. results.title: As AI cheating fears soar, does college matter that much in Korea?
results.content: As someone who never took the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), I found myself asking a question last week while covering anxiety over cheating with artificial intelligence (AI) — a concern that rocked Korea. “Is college really that important in Korea?” My answer is yes. Korean society does push people hard to go to college — and not just any college but a good one. When I was a high school senior, I decided to travel around the world instead of going to college. After a year of working as a cleaner in Australia to fund the trip, I spent another year touring 24 countries. Over the course of those two years, one of the most common refrains from fellow Koreans I met on the road was, “You have to go to college.” True to that advice, Koreans go to college at one of the highest rates in the world. results.title: US poised to unveil new tariffs targeting S. Korea, 15 other trading partners
results.content: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration is poised to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major U.S. trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday, with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected. The results of the investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 are expected as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday, these people said. The U.S. Trade Representative's office is expected to propose new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during Trump's second term. The duties would partly replace global import taxes struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. results.content: WASHINGTON — The U.S. State Department on Tuesday stressed the importance of close cooperation with South Korea following President Lee Jae Myung's nomination of new officials to lead the country's foreign policy, intelligence and inter-Korean affairs. On Monday, Lee nominated Lim Woong-soon, currently the second deputy national security adviser, as foreign minister; former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil as director of the National Intelligence Service (NIS); and former lawmaker Hong Ihk-pyo as unification minister.
